newsitem.title: SPAIN: Part of tobacco pact should be changed - Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Part of tobacco pact should be changed - Clinton.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said Wednesday that a key part of the settlement between U.S. states and tobacco companies would impose an "unreasonable restriction" on tobacco regulation and ought to be changed.

Speaking at a news conference in Madrid after the NATO summit, Clinton said there were many good things in the agreement but he was concerned about the part of the accord dealing with Food and Drug Administration regulation of tobacco. "It seems to me to be a totally unreasonable restriction," he said.

"I have reached only one conclusion about the settlement in terms of what has to be changed -- that portion that restricts the jurisdiction of the FDA in terms of limiting tobacco content in cigarettes or banning it outright," Clinton said.
"I do think that is a change that ought to be made and I cannot believe the tobacco companies would bring down the entire settlement over that," he said.

The agreement between states and tobacco companies says that the FDA could not ban nicotine in cigarettes for a number of years and would have to show that an eventual ban would not create a black market for cigarettes that contain nicotine. Critics of the accord have said this would set impossibly tough standards for the FDA in regulating nicotine.
In return for the limits on FDA authority and some protection from legal liability, tobacco companies agreed to pay $368.5 billion in compensation to the states and for anti-smoking initiatives.
